question: Should OpenClaw adopt the one-Claw-one-new-agent package model and its grouped add/status/update/remove/export contract as an accepted product direction?
rationale: Document correctness cannot decide whether the proposed CLI, manifest, ownership, provenance, shared-package, and upgrade surfaces should become durable OpenClaw contracts.

options.title: Accept the revised contract
options.body: Approve the current agent-centric model, create the implementation issue, transition the RFC to accepted, and require the linked stacks to conform before shipping.

options.title: Narrow the initial contract
options.body: Accept only the add and inspection foundations while deferring update, export, MCP, cron, or shared-package removal semantics to follow-up RFC work.

options.title: Continue incubation
options.body: Keep the RFC draft and experimental while implementation experience resolves remaining compatibility and lifecycle choices.

recommendation.title: Accept the revised contract
recommendation.body: Approve the current agent-centric model, create the implementation issue, transition the RFC to accepted, and require the linked stacks to conform before shipping.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the concrete product-model revision now embodied by the proposal and are the strongest visible discussion-based owner for this specific decision.
